properties.content: Question: how many calories in vegetables list Answer: Most vegetables are low in calories. Many vegetables, especially leafy greens like spinach and lettuce, have very few calories per serving. For example, 100 calories worth of spinach is about 14 cups, according to BODi. Other vegetables like bell peppers, mushrooms, and kale also offer a good amount of volume for 100 calories. Starchy vegetables like corn and potatoes contain more calories per serving. Here's a more detailed look at the calorie content of some common vegetables: Low-Calorie Options (often under 20 calories per cup):: - Arugula: 5 calories per cup. - Lettuce: 5 calories per cup. - Cucumber: 16 calories per cup. - Celery: 14 calories per cup. - Radishes: 19 calories per cup. - Spinach: Very low, with 14 cups making up 100 calories, according to BODi. - Mushrooms: 25 medium mushrooms are about 100 calories, according to BODi. Other Vegetables (calorie counts vary by serving size and type):: - Bell Peppers: 3 medium bell peppers are around 100 calories, according to BODi. - Brussels Sprouts: 13 sprouts are around 100 calories, according to BODi. - Kale: 13 cups are around 100 calories, according to BODi. - Asparagus: 32 medium spears are around 100 calories, according to BODi. - Broccoli: 5 cups of broccoli florets are around 100 calories, according to BODi. - Corn: ⅔ cup is around 100 calories, according to BODi. - Potatoes: ¾ small potato is around 100 calories, according to BODi. Important Considerations:: - Serving Size Matters: Always pay attention to the serving size when looking at calorie information, according to BODi. - Cooking Methods: Cooking methods can also impact calorie count. For example, adding oil or butter will increase the calories. - Starchy vs. Non-starchy: Starchy vegetables like potatoes and corn tend to have more calories than non-starchy vegetables like leafy greens.
